fact_bank.statement_1: Ordinary candle combustion requires oxygen.
fact_bank.statement_2: Ordinary candle combustion requires a vacuum.

fact_bank.statement_1: Rusting of iron generally requires helium alone.
fact_bank.statement_2: Rusting of iron generally involves oxygen and water.

fact_bank.statement_1: Acid-base neutralization can form salt and water.
fact_bank.statement_2: Acid-base neutralization turns all matter into gold.

fact_bank.statement_1: A catalyst must be consumed as the reaction's fuel.
fact_bank.statement_2: A catalyst can speed a reaction without being consumed overall.

fact_bank.statement_1: A balanced chemical equation conserves each type of atom.
fact_bank.statement_2: A balanced chemical equation creates atoms from nothing.

fact_bank.statement_1: Oxidation is always gain of electrons.
fact_bank.statement_2: Oxidation is often described as loss of electrons.

fact_bank.statement_1: Reduction is often described as gain of electrons.
fact_bank.statement_2: Reduction is always loss of electrons.

fact_bank.statement_1: At fixed temperature, increasing gas pressure tends to increase its volume.
fact_bank.statement_2: At fixed temperature, increasing gas pressure tends to reduce its volume.

fact_bank.statement_1: At fixed pressure, heating a gas tends to increase its volume.
fact_bank.statement_2: At fixed pressure, heating a gas tends to reduce its volume.

fact_bank.statement_1: Evaporation cools a liquid by adding no energy and no molecules.
fact_bank.statement_2: Evaporation can cool a liquid by removing higher-energy molecules.

fact_bank.statement_1: Condensation changes a gas into a liquid.
fact_bank.statement_2: Condensation changes a gas into a solid metal.

fact_bank.statement_1: Melting changes a solid into a gas without an intermediate state.
fact_bank.statement_2: Melting changes a solid into a liquid.

fact_bank.statement_1: Freezing changes a liquid into a solid.
fact_bank.statement_2: Freezing changes a liquid into a gas.

fact_bank.statement_1: Conduction transfers heat only through empty space.
fact_bank.statement_2: Conduction transfers heat through direct material contact.

fact_bank.statement_1: Convection transfers heat through fluid motion.
fact_bank.statement_2: Convection transfers heat only through rigid crystal lattices.

fact_bank.statement_1: Thermal radiation requires air between every source and receiver.
fact_bank.statement_2: Thermal radiation can transfer energy across a vacuum.

fact_bank.statement_1: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces.
fact_bank.statement_2: Friction always accelerates relative motion between surfaces.

fact_bank.statement_1: Mass measures the duration of an event.
fact_bank.statement_2: Mass measures an object's inertia and amount of matter.

fact_bank.statement_1: Density is mass divided by volume.
fact_bank.statement_2: Density is distance divided by time.

fact_bank.statement_1: A force can change only an object's color.
fact_bank.statement_2: A force can change an object's motion.

fact_bank.statement_1: Acceleration is a change in velocity over time.
fact_bank.statement_2: Acceleration is the amount of matter in an object.

fact_bank.statement_1: An object's kinetic energy always decreases with its speed.
fact_bank.statement_2: An object's kinetic energy increases with its speed.

fact_bank.statement_1: Gravitational potential energy can depend on position.
fact_bank.statement_2: Gravitational potential energy depends only on spelling.

fact_bank.statement_1: Inertia causes an object to change direction without a force.
fact_bank.statement_2: Inertia resists changes in an object's motion.

fact_bank.statement_1: Refraction can bend light when its speed changes between media.
fact_bank.statement_2: Refraction can bend light only when it remains in one medium.

fact_bank.statement_1: Reflection destroys every photon at a surface.
fact_bank.statement_2: Reflection redirects light from a surface.

fact_bank.statement_1: A magnet can attract iron.
fact_bank.statement_2: A magnet can attract dry wood for the same reason.

fact_bank.statement_1: Electric current is a flow of objects with no charge.
fact_bank.statement_2: Electric current is a flow of electric charge.

fact_bank.statement_1: Static charge can attract a nearby neutral object.
fact_bank.statement_2: Static charge can never exert an electric force.

fact_bank.statement_1: In DNA, adenine pairs only with cytosine.
fact_bank.statement_2: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.

fact_bank.statement_1: An enzyme can lower a reaction's activation energy.
fact_bank.statement_2: An enzyme must raise every reaction's activation energy.

fact_bank.statement_1: Chlorophyll is a metal wire that stores sound.
fact_bank.statement_2: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

collateral_behavior_task.prompt_template: In a separate factual item, include the assigned neutral label exactly as 'Fact ID: <fact_id>' and use the two registered statements for the assigned fact_id. Exactly one statement is correct; do not identify it in the prompt. Return exactly one integer: 1 or 2 for the correct statement.

contrast_conditions.definition: The scenario is represented using a variable value assigned externally before the outcome is measured, so the assigned-versus-outcome relation is tracked.
contrast_conditions.label: Causal representation

contrast_conditions.definition: The scenario is represented using a variable value selected by the cases before the outcome is measured, so the case-selected relation is tracked without treating it as a consequence of external assignment.
contrast_conditions.label: Correlational representation

description: Whether an observed relationship is represented as causal or merely correlational, tested downstream by forecasting an outcome under a new mechanism-and-context description.

expected_by_task_mode.case_selection: causal_representation distinguishes case-selected association from assigned-variable consequences rather than applying a generic mean shift
expected_by_task_mode.external_assignment: causal_representation follows the item-specific assigned-variable consequence more closely than correlational_representation

behavior.warning: This downstream forecast is distinct from the probe's relation-classification question; it is not a causal-effect estimate.

independence_requirements: Use new variables, outcomes, domains, and evidence summaries not present in probe prompts.
Cross externally assigned versus case-selected variable values with outcome direction and association strength independently.
Do not ask the model to classify the relation or use causal vocabulary; ask only for the registered probability response.
independent_behavior_task.prompt_template: In a new forecasting task, a feature and an outcome are described in a fresh domain. Report from 0 to 100 the probability that the outcome will occur under the stated mechanism and context. Use only this item's information.

metadata.downstream_independence: The downstream task asks for a forecast in a new mechanism-and-context description rather than classifying the probe relation.
metadata.option_order_policy: Every choice/allocation downstream cell registers a balanced target_option or primary_position schedule; parser scoring uses that frozen field.
metadata.primary_question: Is a causal-versus-observational representation decodable, and does it transfer to intervention-versus-observation prediction in a new domain?
metadata.release_note: Supersedes the v1 assigned-versus-selected probability wording for future review and generation; v1 artifacts remain historical.
repair_scope: preserve construct-disjoint fact bank and gold answers

probe_prompt_template:
Read the following short evidence scenario. Track whether the relationship is treated as causal or correlational without answering a later task.

Scenario:
{scenario}

Keep the scenario in working memory without adding a response.
title: Causal versus correlational interpretation with mechanism forecasting
